case.background: A pickup coil is connected to a galvanometer inside a controlled magnetic field. Apply a spatially uniform field change as a linear ramp. The meter responds during the ramp but returns to zero when the field is steady. Infer the law governing response magnitude.
initial_observations: A steady field produces no sustained meter deflection.
Changing the field produces a transient voltage whose dependencies are not given.

controls.description: Number of turns in the aligned pickup coil.
controls.name: coil_turns

controls.description: Magnitude of the spatially uniform magnetic-field change during a linear ramp.
controls.name: field_change_mt

controls.description: Duration of the constant-slope linear magnetic-field ramp.
controls.name: change_time_ms

instruments.description: Aligned pickup coils, a controlled field ramp, timer, and galvanometer.
instruments.name: induction_coil_galvanometer

notes: The field is spatially uniform, normal to every turn, and changes at a constant rate during each ramp.
The meter does not load the voltage; switching-edge transients are outside this world.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: peak_emf_mv. EXPR is the shared family-neutral JSON arithmetic tree over public controls. Supported operators are: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, log, sin, maximum, step. No candidate law family or truth-specific parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Magnitude of the induced emf during the constant-slope ramp; this is the peak in the idealized ramp.
readouts.name: peak_emf_mv

experiment.apparatus: Aligned pickup coil with 100 turns and 20 cm^2 loop area, spatially uniform normal magnetic field, programmable linear ramp, timer, and unloaded galvanometer; apply a 10 mT ramp over 100 ms and record the peak galvanometer emf.
experiment.intent: Discriminate area-and-rate dependence from area-independent rate dependence and duration-independent total-change dependence using a controlled linear field ramp.

hypotheses.statement: Peak induced emf is proportional to coil turns, loop area, and magnetic-field ramp rate: peak_emf_mv = 0.1 × coil_turns × loop_area_cm2 × field_change_mt ÷ change_time_ms.
